p.src: Now Xifeng ordered the women who had been on night duty to be bound and sent to the military authorities for questioning. They fell to their knees and begged for mercy. Lin Zhixiao and Jia Yun said to them, “It is no use pleading with us. The masters charged us with guarding the house. Had nothing happened, we should have counted ourselves fortunate; now that something has, every one of us, high and low, is to blame. Who can save you? If the culprit truly is Zhou Rui’s godson, then beginning with Madam herself, no one inside or outside the household will escape suspicion.” Xifeng said breathlessly, “All this was ordained by fate. What is the use of talking to them? Just take them away. Tell the military authorities that the stolen articles truly belonged to the Old Lady; the masters will have to be consulted before the particulars can be known. Once we have sent word and asked the masters to return, a proper inventory of the losses will naturally be drawn up and delivered. We shall make the same report to the civil authorities.” Jia Yun and Lin Zhixiao assented and went out.

p.src: Xichun had not uttered a word, but now she wept, “I have never even heard of such a thing. Why did it have to happen while the two of us were in charge? How can I face anyone when Master and Madam return tomorrow? They said they were entrusting the household to us, and now things have come to this. How can I go on living?” “Do you think we wished this to happen?” said Xifeng. “The night watchwomen are right there to answer for it.” “You can still explain yourself,” said Xichun, “and besides, you are ill. I have nothing I can say. It was all my eldest sister-in-law’s doing. She urged Madam to put me in charge of the house. How can I ever show my face again?” At this she burst into bitter tears again. Xifeng said, “My dear girl, you must not think like this. If it is a question of losing face, we are all in the same plight. If you indulge in such foolish thoughts, I shall be unable to bear it either.”

p.src: While they were speaking, they suddenly heard someone shouting in the courtyard outside, “I have always said that meddlesome women and religious busybodies are the worst people to admit. At the Zhen residence we never allow any of them through the door, but it seems this household pays no attention to such matters. The Old Lady’s funeral procession had only just left yesterday when a nun from some convent or other insisted on coming here. I shouted that she was not to be admitted, but the old woman at the inner gate cursed me and begged and pleaded until the nun was let in. That inner gate was opened one moment and shut the next, and I had no idea what was going on. I felt uneasy and did not dare sleep; then, during the fourth watch, the uproar began here. When I came to call at the gate, it would not open. Hearing the commotion grow urgent, I broke it open, saw someone standing in the western courtyard, and chased him off and beat him to death. Only today did I learn that these are Fourth Miss’s rooms. That nun was inside, and before dawn today she slipped away. Surely it was she who let the thieves in!” When Ping’er and the others heard this, they said, “Who is that ill-mannered creature? How dare he bellow such nonsense outside while the young ladies and mistresses are all here?” Xifeng said, “You heard him mention ‘our Zhen residence.’ Could it be that loathsome fellow recommended to us by the Zhen family?” Xichun had understood every word, and her heart grew even more distressed. Xifeng then asked Xichun, “What does that man mean with his wild talk about a nun? Did you have some nun staying in your quarters?” Xichun explained that Miaoyu had come to see her and that she had asked her to stay, play chess, and keep her company through the night. “Miaoyu?” said Xifeng. “How could she possibly do such a thing? There is not a word of truth in it. Still, it will be awkward if that hateful creature’s shouting brings the matter to Master’s attention.” The more Xichun thought about it, the more frightened she became, and she rose to leave. Though Xifeng herself could scarcely remain seated, she feared Xichun might cause some mishap in her terror and had no choice but to ask her not to leave yet. “We should first see that the articles the thieves left behind are gathered up and appoint someone to guard them; then we can go.” Ping’er said, “We dare not gather anything up. We had better wait until the officials come and inspect the scene. All we can do is keep watch over it. But I wonder whether anyone has gone to inform Master?” “Send an old woman to inquire,” said Xifeng. Presently the woman returned and reported, “Lin Zhixiao cannot get away: the household servants must remain to assist with the inspection, and some of them would be unable to explain matters clearly. Second Master Yun has already gone instead.” Xifeng nodded and sat with Xichun, both consumed by anxiety.

p.src: As for the band of thieves, they had originally been recruited by He San and his companions. After stealing and plundering a great quantity of gold, silver, and valuables, they had passed the loot outside. When they saw that they were being pursued and realized that their pursuers were all ineffectual fellows, they meant to rob the rooms on the western side as well. Looking through the window, they saw two beauties beneath the lamplight within: a young lady and a nun. Reckless of life and limb, the thieves were suddenly seized by evil desire and were about to kick their way inside; only when they saw Bao Yong coming after them did they flee with their plunder. Only He San was nowhere to be seen. For the time being, the others hid in a receiver’s den. When they made inquiries the next day, they learned that He San had been beaten to death and that reports had already been lodged with both the civil and military authorities. Realizing they could not remain hidden there, they discussed joining a band of pirates as soon as possible. If they delayed until the wanted notices were circulated, they would no longer be able to pass the checkpoints and ferries.

p.src: One exceptionally bold fellow among them said, “We may be leaving, but I cannot bear to give up that nun. She really is beautiful. I wonder which convent that little novice belongs to?” Another man said, “Ah! I remember now. She must be the nun from some place called Green Bower Hermitage in the Jia family’s garden. Was she not the one people outside said had some involvement with a certain Second Master Bao of that family the year before last, and who later came down with lovesickness for some reason and had to send for doctors and take medicine?” On hearing this, the first man said, “We shall lie low for today. We will ask our chief to borrow some money and procure the clothes and equipment of travelling merchants, then tomorrow, at the dawn bell, we shall slip through the pass one after another. Wait for me at Twenty-Li Slope beyond the pass.” Having settled their plans, the thieves divided the loot and dispersed. No more need be said of them for now.

p.src: Now Jia Zheng and the others escorted the coffin to the temple, where it was duly laid to rest, after which the relatives and friends dispersed. Jia Zheng kept vigil beside the coffin in an outer chamber, while Ladies Xing and Wang and the others stayed within; all they did throughout the night was weep. On the following day, offerings were presented anew. Just as the meal was being set out, Jia Yun came in, kowtowed before the old lady's spirit, then hurried over to Jia Zheng, knelt and paid his respects. Gasping for breath, he reported that thieves had broken in the previous night and stolen everything from the old lady's principal apartments, that Bao Yong had killed one of them while pursuing the gang, and that the matter had already been reported to both the civil and military authorities. Jia Zheng stared blankly at the news. Ladies Xing and Wang and the others inside heard it too. They were frightened out of their wits and could not utter a word, but only wept. After a while Jia Zheng asked how the inventory of losses had been drawn up. Jia Yun replied, “No one at home knows what was there, so no list has yet been made.” “That is just as well,” said Jia Zheng. “Our property has already been confiscated once; if we list anything too valuable, we may instead lay ourselves open to charges. Send for Lian at once.”

p.src: Jia Lian had taken Baoyu and the others elsewhere to make offerings and had not yet returned, so Jia Zheng sent someone to fetch him back. When Jia Lian heard what had happened, he leapt about in agitation. The moment he saw Yun, he disregarded Jia Zheng's presence and berated him fiercely: “You worthless wretch, unfit for any advancement! I entrusted you with so grave a duty—supervising the night watch and patrols. Were you dead or what? And you still have the face to come and tell me!” As he spoke, he spat several times in Jia Yun's face. Jia Yun stood with his hands at his sides, not daring to answer a word. “There is no use scolding him now,” said Jia Zheng. Jia Lian then knelt and asked, “What are we to do?” “There is nothing else to be done,” said Jia Zheng. “We can only report it to the authorities and have the thieves pursued. But there is one difficulty: we have not touched anything the old lady left behind. You said you needed silver, but she had been dead only a few days, and who could bring himself to lay hands on her personal funds? My original intention was to settle the accounts after the funeral, repay what we owed, and use what remained to acquire burial lands both here and in the south; as for the other belongings, no inventory was ever made. Now the civil and military authorities are demanding a list of the losses. If we put down several valuable articles, it may cause trouble; yet if we state so much gold and silver and so many garments and ornaments, we have no exact figures, and we cannot submit a false account. It is astonishing—you seem to have become a different man. Why can you no longer manage even a matter like this? And what do you mean by kneeling there?” Jia Lian dared not reply. He could only rise and make to leave. Jia Zheng called after him, “Where are you going?” Jia Lian knelt again and said, “I shall hurry back, put everything in order, and then return to report.” Jia Zheng gave a snort, and Jia Lian lowered his head. “Go inside and tell your mother,” said Jia Zheng. “Take one or two of the old lady's maids with you and have them think carefully before drawing up the list.” Jia Lian knew full well that all the old lady's belongings had been managed by Yuanyang; now that she was dead, whom could they ask? Even if they asked Zhenzhu, how could she and the others remember everything clearly? But he dared not object; he repeatedly assented, rose, and went inside. Ladies Xing and Wang reproached him at length as well, then told him to hurry back and demand of those guarding the house, “How will you face us tomorrow?” Jia Lian could only agree and go out. He ordered a carriage harnessed to take Hupo and the others into the city, while he himself mounted a mule and, accompanied by several pages, sped home as if on wings. Jia Yun did not dare report again to Jia Zheng. Keeping himself half-turned in deference, he slowly slipped away, mounted his horse, and rode after Jia Lian. Nothing further happened on the way.

p.src: When they reached home, Lin Zhixiao paid his respects and followed Jia Lian straight inside. Jia Lian entered the old lady's principal apartments and saw Xifeng and Xichun there. Though inwardly furious, he could not give vent to his anger, and asked Lin Zhixiao, “Have the authorities inspected the place?” Knowing himself to be at fault, Lin Zhixiao knelt and replied, “Both the civil and military authorities have inspected the premises. They examined the thieves' tracks in and out, and examined the corpse as well.” Startled, Jia Lian asked, “What corpse did they examine?” Lin Zhixiao then told him that the thief Bao Yong had killed appeared to be Zhou Rui's godson. “Call Yun,” said Jia Lian. Jia Yun came in and knelt to receive his orders. Jia Lian asked, “When you saw the master, why did you not report that Zhou Rui's godson had turned thief and been killed by Bao Yong?” “The night watchmen said it looked like him,” replied Jia Yun, “but I feared they might be mistaken, so I did not report it.” “What a muddle-headed fool you are!” said Jia Lian. “Had you told me, we could have brought Zhou Rui to identify him and known at once.” Lin Zhixiao reported, “The authorities have now placed the corpse at the marketplace for public identification.” “That is another piece of folly,” said Jia Lian. “What family would claim a man who became a thief and was beaten to death? Do they mean to demand that someone pay with his life?” Lin Zhixiao replied, “There is no need for anyone else to identify him. I myself recognize him.” Hearing this, Jia Lian thought, “Yes, of course. Was it not someone from Zhou Rui's household whom Cousin Zhen wanted beaten that year?” Lin Zhixiao added, “He once fought with Bao Er, and I saw him then.” This made Jia Lian angrier still, and he wanted to have the night watchmen beaten. Lin Zhixiao pleaded, “Please calm your anger, Second Master. Once those night watchmen had been assigned their duties, how would they dare shirk them? It is simply the rule in your household that no man dares pass the third gate. Even we servants dare not enter unless summoned from within. Outside, Brother Yun and I made inspections at every moment. We saw that the third gate was tightly shut and that not one of the outer gates had been opened. The thieves came through the rear passageway.” “What of the women keeping watch inside?” asked Jia Lian. Lin Zhixiao reported that the women who had taken turns on night watch had been bound on Madam's orders and were awaiting the Second Master's interrogation. Jia Lian asked again, “Where is Bao Yong?” “He has gone back to the Garden,” replied Lin Zhixiao. “Go and summon him,” said Jia Lian. The pages brought Bao Yong in. Jia Lian said, “It was fortunate you were here. Without you, I fear they would have plundered everything in every room.” Bao Yong said nothing. Xichun grew anxious, fearing that he might reveal that matter. Xifeng, too, dared not speak. Just then someone outside announced, “Sister Hupo and the others have returned.”

p.src: Jia Lian ordered the servants to take stock of what the thieves had left behind. Only some clothes, bolts of cloth, and the cash chests remained untouched; everything else was gone. Jia Lian grew still more anxious, thinking, “I have not yet paid for the awnings and poles outside, or settled the kitchen expenses. What shall I use to pay them tomorrow?” For a while he remained there, lost in thought. Amber and the others went inside and wept for a while. Seeing all the trunks and cupboards standing open, they could hardly remember everything that had been in them, so they made guesses at random, drew up a largely conjectural list of losses, and had it sent at once to both the civil and military authorities. Jia Lian then assigned men to keep watch through the night. Xifeng and Xichun each returned to her own room. Jia Lian dared not rest at home, nor did he have time to reproach Xifeng; instead, he mounted his horse and hurried straight out of the city. Meanwhile, fearing that Xichun might do herself some harm, Xifeng sent Fenger over to comfort her.

p.src: By the fourth watch, they saw that only a single vigil lamp remained alight inside and that Miaoyu was sitting alone in meditation on a rush cushion. After a while, she sighed and said, “When I came from the Xuanzang Hills to the capital, I had hoped to make something of a name for myself. But since I was invited here, I cannot very well go and live elsewhere. Yesterday I went with the best of intentions to see Fourth Miss, only to be subjected to that fool’s insolence, and then I suffered a terrible fright during the night. Since returning today, I cannot sit steadily even on this cushion; my flesh keeps twitching and my heart pounds with alarm.” She was accustomed to meditating alone and had refused to let anyone keep her company that day. Little did she know that by the fifth watch she would begin to shiver. She was just about to call someone when she heard a noise outside the window. Remembering what had happened the previous night, she became even more frightened and could not help calling out. But none of the old women answered. As she sat there, she felt a fragrant vapor penetrate the crown of her head. Her hands and feet went numb, leaving her unable to move, and no words would come from her mouth, which made her still more frantic within. Then she saw a man enter carrying a gleaming knife. Miaoyu’s mind was perfectly clear, though she could not move. Supposing he meant to kill her, she steeled herself and was no longer afraid. But instead, the man thrust the knife behind his back, freed his hands, gently lifted Miaoyu, took liberties with her for a while, and then hoisted her onto his back. By then Miaoyu felt as though she were drunk or delirious. Poor girl, pure and immaculate beyond compare! Overcome by the brigand’s stupefying incense, she was left helpless in his hands and carried away.

p.src: The thief carried Miaoyu to the rear wall of the garden, set up a rope ladder, climbed to the top, and jumped down outside. His accomplices already had a carriage waiting outside the garden. The man laid Miaoyu inside it, boldly raised a lantern bearing an official title, had the barriers opened, and hurried to the city gate just as it was being unlocked. The gate officers assumed they were leaving the city on official business and did not stop to question them. Once outside the city, the thieves whipped their horses on to Twenty-Li Slope, where they met up with the other brigands; then they split into separate groups and fled southward toward the coast. Whether Miaoyu, after being abducted, submitted to defilement or resisted and died, no one knows; her fate is unknown, and it would be difficult to speculate rashly.

p.src: Now there was a nun at Green Lattice Convent who attended Miaoyu. She slept in a quiet room at the rear, and at the fifth watch she heard voices in front, but merely supposed that Miaoyu was restless during meditation. Later she heard a man’s footsteps and the rattling of doors and windows. She wanted to get up and investigate, but her body felt weak and she could scarcely bring herself to speak. Hearing no sound from Miaoyu, she could only lie there wide-eyed and listen. At daybreak her mind finally cleared. She put on her clothes, told a lay sister to prepare Miaoyu’s tea and hot water, and went to the front to see her. To her astonishment, Miaoyu had vanished without a trace, and the doors and windows stood wide open. She was bewildered. Recalling the suspicious noises of the previous night, she said, “Where could she have gone so early?” When she stepped into the courtyard, she saw a rope ladder leaning against the wall and, on the ground, a knife sheath and a sash. “This is terrible!” she cried. “The thieves burned stupefying incense last night!” She hurriedly roused everyone to investigate, but the convent gate was still tightly shut. The old women and maidservants all said, “We were overcome by coal fumes last night, and this morning none of us can even get up. Why are you calling us at such an early hour?” The nun said, “No one knows where our mistress has gone.” The others said, “She is meditating in the Guanyin Hall.” “You are still dreaming,” said the nun. “Come and see for yourselves.” The others, knowing nothing of what had happened, now became alarmed too. They opened the convent gate and searched throughout the garden. “Perhaps she has gone to Fourth Miss’s quarters,” they suggested.

p.src: They went and knocked at the side gate, only to receive another scolding from Baoyong. They said, “No one knows where our Mistress Miaoyu went last night, so we have come to look for her. Please, sir, have the side gate opened and simply ask whether she came here or not.” Baoyong said, “Your mistress brought the thieves here to rob us. Now that they have got what they wanted, she has gone off with them to enjoy herself.” “Amitabha Buddha!” they exclaimed. “Anyone who says such things had better beware of falling into the hell where tongues are cut out!” Baoyong said angrily, “Nonsense! If you keep making a commotion, I shall beat you.” Smiling placatingly, they pleaded, “Please, sir, have the gate opened and let us look. If she is not here, we shall not dare trouble your master again.” Baoyong said, “If you do not believe me, go and look. If she is not there, I shall have words with you when you return.” With that, Baoyong had the side gate opened, and they went to Xichun’s quarters in search of Miaoyu.

p.src: Xichun was already sunk in melancholy, thinking, “After Miaoyu left early this morning, I wonder whether she heard what that man Bao said. I fear we may have offended her again, and that she will never come here anymore. Then I shall have no true friend left. Besides, as matters stand, I can scarcely face anyone. My parents died young, my sister-in-law dislikes me, and though the Old Lady used to show me some affection, she too is dead now. Left all alone and wretched, what is to become of me?” She went on thinking, “Second Sister Yingchun was tormented to death, Cousin Shi is tending a sick husband, and Third Sister has gone far away. All this was ordained by fate, and none of them could choose for herself. Only Miaoyu is as free as an idle cloud or a wild crane, bound by nothing. If I could follow her example, I should count myself exceedingly fortunate. But I am the daughter of a noble house—how could I ever have my wish? I have already incurred grave blame for what happened while I was left in charge of the house. How can I have the face to remain here? And I fear the ladies do not understand what is in my heart. What will become of me in the end?” As these thoughts passed through her mind, she resolved to cut off her black tresses and become a nun. When Caiping and the others heard, they hurried in to dissuade her, only to find that she had already cut off half her hair. Caiping grew still more frantic and cried, “Before one trouble is settled, another arises! What are we to do now?”

p.src: In the midst of the commotion, the Daoist women from Miaoyu’s convent arrived looking for her. When Caiping asked what had brought them, she was startled to hear that Miaoyu had left early the previous morning and had not returned. Hearing this from inside, Xichun hastily asked, “Where could she have gone?” The women related everything: the noises they had heard during the night, how they had been overcome by charcoal fumes, how Miaoyu was nowhere to be found that morning, and how a rope ladder and a knife sheath had been discovered in the convent. Xichun was torn between alarm and doubt. Recalling what Bao Yong had said the day before, she thought that the bandits might have seen Miaoyu and carried her off the previous night. “But she has always been fiercely pure and proud. Surely she would never cling to life at the cost of her honour? How was it that none of you heard anything?” “Of course we heard!” they replied. “But though our eyes were open, not one of us could utter a word. The thieves must have burned some stupefying incense. Miss Miaoyu must likewise have been drugged speechless; and besides, there were surely many thieves, threatening her with knives and staves. How could she have dared to cry out?” As they were speaking, Bao Yong began shouting again at the inner gate: “Drive those wretched old women out at once, and shut the inner gate!” Afraid she would be blamed, Caiping had no choice but to send the women away and order the gate shut. Xichun’s anguish only deepened. Yet after Caiping and the others repeatedly reasoned with her in all courtesy, she gathered up the half of her black hair that remained. They agreed that nothing should be said publicly; even if Miaoyu had been abducted, they would pretend to know nothing and wait until the master and ladies returned. In her heart, however, Xichun firmly resolved to enter religious life. For the moment, we shall leave her there.

p.src: Meanwhile, Jia Lian returned to Iron Threshold Temple and reported that he had gone home, questioned those who had kept watch that night, drawn up a list of the stolen property, and submitted the case to the authorities. Jia Zheng asked, “How did you draw up the list?” Jia Lian presented the inventory of items that Amber could remember and said, “The things bestowed by the Imperial Consort have been clearly marked on this list. There are also some rare objects that it would be inconvenient to include. When my mourning period is over, I shall go out and engage someone to investigate carefully; they are bound to turn up.” Jia Zheng was satisfied and merely nodded without speaking. Jia Lian went inside to see Ladies Xing and Wang and proposed, “We ought to persuade Master to return home as soon as possible; otherwise everything will remain a hopeless tangle.” Lady Xing said, “Indeed. We ourselves are living in constant fear here.” Jia Lian replied, “We would not dare suggest it ourselves, but Second Master will follow your wishes, Madam.” Lady Xing then discussed the matter with Lady Wang, and they came to an agreement.

p.src: After another night, Jia Zheng too became uneasy and sent Baoyu inside with this message: “Please ask the ladies to return home today and come back in two or three days. The male servants have already been assigned; please have the ladies appoint the women who are to remain.” Lady Xing appointed Parrot and several others to keep vigil beside the coffin and placed Zhou Rui’s wife and some others in overall charge; everyone else, high and low, was to return home. For a time there was great bustle as carriages were harnessed and horses saddled. Jia Zheng and the others took leave before Grandmother Jia’s spirit tablet, and everyone wept once more.

p.src: They had all risen and were about to leave when they saw that Concubine Zhao was still prostrate on the floor and would not get up. Concubine Zhou supposed that she was still weeping and went over to help her up. To her horror, Concubine Zhao’s mouth was covered in white foam, her eyes stared rigidly upward, and her tongue protruded, giving the whole household a terrible fright. Jia Huan rushed over, shouting wildly. Concubine Zhao came to and said, “I am not going back. I shall follow the Old Lady home to the South.” The others said, “What need would the Old Lady have of you?” Concubine Zhao said, “I served the Old Lady all my life, yet the Elder Master still would not leave me alone and resorted to spirits and sorcery to plot against me. I once hoped to rely on Mother Ma to vent my spite. I spent a great deal of silver for nothing, yet did not manage to kill a single one of them. If I go back now, who knows who will scheme against me next?” On hearing this, everyone immediately concluded that Yuanyang’s spirit had possessed her. Ladies Xing and Wang merely watched in silence. Only Caiyun and the others pleaded on Concubine Zhao’s behalf: “Sister Yuanyang, you chose to die of your own accord. What has that to do with Concubine Zhao? Please release her.” With Lady Xing present, however, they dared say nothing more. Concubine Zhao said, “I am not Yuanyang. She has long since ascended to the realm of the immortals. The King of Hell has sent officers to take me away and question me about the case in which I used black magic with Mother Ma.” Then she called out, “Dear Second Mistress Lian, please put in a good word for me before Master here. Though I may have been bad for a thousand days, surely there was one day when I was good. Dear Second Mistress, my own dear Second Mistress, I never meant to harm you. I lost my senses for a moment and listened to that old harlot.”

p.src: In the midst of the commotion, Jia Zheng sent someone in to summon Huan. The old women went back and reported, “Aunt Zhao has been possessed by an evil spirit, and Third Master is watching over her.” Jia Zheng said, “Nonsense. We shall leave first.” Accordingly, the gentlemen and the others returned first. Aunt Zhao continued to rave there, and for the moment no one could bring her round. Lady Xing, fearing that she might blurt out something else, said, “Leave several more people here to watch her. Let us go ahead, and once we reach the city we shall send a doctor out to examine her.” Lady Wang had never liked her and likewise washed her hands of the matter. Baochai was kindhearted by nature. Though she remembered how Aunt Zhao had tried to harm Baoyu, she could not bring herself to abandon her; in private, she asked Aunt Zhou to remain and look after her. Aunt Zhou was a good woman too, and readily agreed. Li Wan said, “I shall stay here too.” Lady Wang replied, “There is no need.” Everyone then prepared to leave. Jia Huan asked hastily, “Am I to stay here too?” Lady Wang spat in disgust, “You witless fool! Your own mother may live or die, and you know nothing of it—yet you still mean to leave?” Jia Huan dared say no more. Baoyu said, “My good brother, you cannot leave. When I reach the city, I shall send someone to see how you are.” With that, they all boarded their carriages and went home. Only Aunt Zhao, Jia Huan, Yingwu, and a few others remained at the temple.

p.src: Jia Zheng, Lady Xing, and the others arrived home one after another, went to the principal apartments, and wept for a while. Lin Zhixiao led the household servants in to pay their respects, and they knelt before them. Jia Zheng barked, “Go away! I shall question you tomorrow!” Xifeng had fainted several times that day and was quite unable to come out to receive them. Only Xichun appeared, her face full of shame. Lady Xing ignored her; Lady Wang treated her as usual, while Li Wan and Baochai took her hands and spoke a few words to her. Only Madam You remarked, “You have had a trying time, miss, looking after everything for so many days!” Xichun made no reply; her face merely flushed dark crimson. Baochai tugged at Madam You and gave her a meaningful look, whereupon Madam You and the others withdrew to their own rooms. Jia Zheng looked around briefly and sighed without speaking. He went to his study, sat down on the bare floor, and summoned Jia Lian, Jia Rong, and Jia Yun to give them a few instructions. Baoyu wished to join Jia Zheng in the study and keep him company, but Jia Zheng said, “There is no need.” Lan remained with his mother, and the night passed without incident.

p.src: Early the next morning, Lin Zhixiao entered the study and knelt down. Jia Zheng questioned him fully about the successive robberies, and he implicated Zhou Rui, adding, “The yamen has arrested Bao Er. Articles listed among the stolen goods were found on him. They are putting him to the press now, hoping to force him to reveal the whole band of thieves.” On hearing this, Jia Zheng flew into a rage. “A house-slave repays his master's kindness by bringing thieves in to rob him! This is outright rebellion!” He immediately ordered men to go outside the city, bind Zhou Rui, and deliver him to the yamen for interrogation. Lin Zhixiao remained on his knees, not daring to rise. Jia Zheng said, “Why are you still kneeling there?” Lin Zhixiao said, “Your servant deserves death. I beg your lordship to show mercy.” As he spoke, Lai Da and the other stewards came forward to pay their respects and presented the funeral account books. Jia Zheng said, “Hand them to Second Master Lian. Have him settle the accounts and report back.” Then he shouted at Lin Zhixiao to get up and leave.

On hearing this, Jia Zheng flew into a rage. “A house-slave repays his master's kindness by bringing thieves in to rob him! This is outright rebellion!”
He immediately ordered men to go outside the city, bind Zhou Rui, and deliver him to the yamen for interrogation.
Lin Zhixiao remained on his knees, not daring to rise.
Jia Zheng said, “Why are you still kneeling there?”
Lin Zhixiao said, “Your servant deserves death. I beg your lordship to show mercy.”
As he spoke, Lai Da and the other stewards came forward to pay their respects and presented the funeral account books.
Jia Zheng said, “Hand them to Second Master Lian. Have him settle the accounts and report back.”
Then he shouted at Lin Zhixiao to get up and leave.

p.src: Jia Lian dropped to one knee beside Jia Zheng and said something to him. Jia Zheng glared at him. “Nonsense! This concerns the Old Lady's funeral. Since the silver was stolen by thieves, are the servants to be forced to replace it from their own pockets?” Jia Lian flushed and dared not speak. He rose but did not dare move. Jia Zheng asked, “How is your wife?” Jia Lian knelt again and said, “It appears she will not recover.” Jia Zheng sighed. “I never imagined that the fortunes of our house would decline to such a pass! Moreover, Brother Huan's mother is still ill at the temple, and no one knows what ails her. Do any of you know?” Jia Lian still dared not speak. Jia Zheng said, “Send word out. Have someone take a doctor there to examine her.” Jia Lian hastily assented and withdrew, then ordered someone to take a doctor to Iron Threshold Temple to examine Aunt Zhao. Whether she lived or died will be told in the next chapter.
